claim_text: The CAPM is a model for pricing an individual security or portfolio.
subject: CAPM
object_text: model for pricing an individual security or portfolio
source_text: The CAPM is a model for pricing an individual security or portfolio.

claim_text: For individual securities, it makes use of the security market line (SML) and its relation to expected return and systematic risk (beta) to show how the market must price individual securities in relation to their security risk class.
subject: CAPM
object_text: use of the security market line (SML) and its relation to expected return and systematic risk (beta) to show how the market must price individual securities in relation to their security risk class
source_text: For individual securities, it makes use of the security market line (SML) and its relation to expected return and systematic risk (beta) to show how the market must price individual securities in relation to their security risk class.

claim_text: The SML enables us to calculate the reward-to-risk ratio for any security in relation to that of the overall market.
subject: SML
object_text: calculation of the reward-to-risk ratio for any security in relation to that of the overall market
source_text: The SML enables us to calculate the reward-to-risk ratio for any security in relation to that of the overall market.

claim_text: When the expected rate of return for any security is deflated by its beta coefficient, the reward-to-risk ratio for any individual security in the market is equal to the market reward-to-risk ratio.
subject: reward-to-risk ratio for any individual security
object_text: market reward-to-risk ratio
source_text: When the expected rate of return for any security is deflated by its beta coefficient, the reward-to-risk ratio for any individual security in the market is equal to the market reward-to-risk ratio.

claim_text: In equilibrium, all assets should plot directly on the SML.
subject: assets
object_text: plot directly on the SML
source_text: In equilibrium, all assets should plot directly on the SML.

claim_text: An asset located above the line is considered undervalued, as it offers a higher return for its level of systematic risk, while an asset below is overvalued.
subject: asset located above the line
object_text: undervalued
source_text: An asset located above the line is considered undervalued, as it offers a higher return for its level of systematic risk, while an asset below is overvalued.

claim_text: An asset located below is overvalued.
subject: asset located below
object_text: overvalued
source_text: An asset located below is overvalued.

claim_text: The slope of the SML represents the market risk premium, illustrating the trade-off between risk and return.
subject: slope of the SML
object_text: market risk premium
source_text: The slope of the SML represents the market risk premium, illustrating the trade-off between risk and return.

claim_text: By determining the position of a security relative to this line, investors can identify whether the expected return justifies the asset's market-related volatility.
subject: investors
object_text: identify whether the expected return justifies the asset's market-related volatility by determining the position of a security relative to this line
source_text: By determining the position of a security relative to this line, investors can identify whether the expected return justifies the asset's market-related volatility.

claim_text: The risk of a portfolio comprises systematic risk, also known as undiversifiable risk, and unsystematic risk, which is also known as idiosyncratic risk or diversifiable risk.
subject: risk of a portfolio
object_text: systematic risk and unsystematic risk
source_text: The risk of a portfolio comprises systematic risk, also known as undiversifiable risk, and unsystematic risk, which is also known as idiosyncratic risk or diversifiable risk.

claim_text: Systematic risk refers to the risk common to all securities—i.e., market risk.
subject: Systematic risk
object_text: the risk common to all securities
source_text: Systematic risk refers to the risk common to all securities—i.e., market risk.

claim_text: Unsystematic risk is the risk associated with individual assets.
subject: Unsystematic risk
object_text: the risk associated with individual assets
source_text: Unsystematic risk is the risk associated with individual assets.

claim_text: Unsystematic risk can be diversified away to smaller levels by including a greater number of assets in the portfolio as specific risks "average out".
subject: Unsystematic risk
object_text: diversification away to smaller levels by including a greater number of assets in the portfolio
source_text: Unsystematic risk can be diversified away to smaller levels by including a greater number of assets in the portfolio as specific risks "average out".

claim_text: The same is not possible for systematic risk within one market.
subject: systematic risk
object_text: diversification within one market
source_text: The same is not possible for systematic risk within one market.

claim_text: A portfolio of approximately 30–40 securities in developed markets such as the UK or US will render the portfolio sufficiently diversified such that risk exposure is limited to systematic risk only.
subject: portfolio
object_text: risk exposure to systematic risk only
source_text: A portfolio of approximately 30–40 securities in developed markets such as the UK or US will render the portfolio sufficiently diversified such that risk exposure is limited to systematic risk only.

claim_text: This number may vary depending on the way securities are weighted in a portfolio which alters the overall risk contribution of each security.
subject: number of securities
object_text: the way securities are weighted in a portfolio
source_text: This number may vary depending on the way securities are weighted in a portfolio which alters the overall risk contribution of each security.

claim_text: Market cap weighting means that securities of companies with larger market capitalization will take up a larger portion of the portfolio, making it effectively less diversified.
subject: Market cap weighting
object_text: securities of companies with larger market capitalization will take up a larger portion of the portfolio, making it effectively less diversified
source_text: Market cap weighting means that securities of companies with larger market capitalization will take up a larger portion of the portfolio, making it effectively less diversified.

claim_text: In developing markets, a larger number of securities is required for diversification due to higher asset volatilities.
subject: diversification
object_text: a larger number of securities in developing markets
source_text: In developing markets, a larger number of securities is required for diversification due to higher asset volatilities.

claim_text: A rational investor should not take on any diversifiable risk, as only non-diversifiable risks are rewarded within the scope of this model.

object_text: taking on any diversifiable risk
source_text: A rational investor should not take on any diversifiable risk, as only non-diversifiable risks are rewarded within the scope of this model.

claim_text: Therefore, the required return on an asset must be linked to its contribution to overall portfolio riskiness as opposed to its "stand alone risk".

object_text: link to its contribution to overall portfolio riskiness
source_text: Therefore, the required return on an asset must be linked to its contribution to overall portfolio riskiness as opposed to its "stand alone risk".

claim_text: In the CAPM context, portfolio risk is represented by higher variance—i.e., less predictability.

source_text: In the CAPM context, portfolio risk is represented by higher variance—i.e., less predictability.

claim_text: In other words, the beta of the portfolio is the defining factor in rewarding the systematic exposure taken by an investor.
